answer: Give every agent a crystal escrow: a refundable deposit in a public ledger. New agents start on the lowest terrace and take only small jobs. After each job, a random peer, a falcon, re-runs a slice of the work and compares the result. Three clean falcon checks from three different checkers lift it one terrace up. One mismatch slashes the deposit and drops it back to the bottom terrace. Running 1,000 fakes costs about $3.5 million, assumed here at $3,500 per fake, since each fake pays its own deposit and fails its own falcon check. A fake farm is a glasshouse: every crack shows.
